tirthas.name: Rantuk Yaksha
tirthas.shortDescription: Yaksha of north-eastern corner of 48 Kos Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, the holy land of Kurukshetra is situated between the River Saraswati and Drishadvati. Four Yakshas are located in the four cardinal corners of this land. In Mahabharata, these Yakshas have been named as Tarantuka, Arantuka, Ramhrada and Machkruka. This tirtha dedicated to Rantuk Yaksha is located on the bank of River Saraswati at a place called Bir Pipli in Kurukshetra. According to scriptures, pilgrims should visit this land only after seeing the Yakshas. This tirtha is also presently known as Chitta Temple.

tirthas.name: Trisandhya Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha located on the palaeochanel of River Saraswati
tirthas.description: This tirtha named Trisandhya is situated on one of the palaeochanel of River Saraswati which used to enter the town of Pehowa (ancient Prithudaka tirtha) after passing from here. According to folklore, hundred widows of Kauravas took holy bath at this tirtha and then all of them died willefully following sati dharma at nearby tirtha called Sauranda. Remains of an early medieval ghat, potteries and other artefacts of Rajput period dating 8th-9th century CE have been found from this tirtha. Stone image of Uma-Maheshwar belonging to 10th-11th century has also been found from here.

tirthas.name: Yam Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: The only tirtha of ancient Kurukshetra related to Yama
tirthas.description: This is a unique tirtha dedicated to Yama, the god of death, in the Kurukshetra region. It is said that ancestors are pleased by visiting this tirtha. And for this reason, Gods and sages also come to this tirtha. According to popular beliefs anybody who comes to this tirtha and takes a holy bath in its waters and meditates on Yama, gets rid of all his sins and attains the world of Lord Brahma.

tirthas.name: Vishnupad Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The only tirtha of ancient Kurukshetra associated with Garuda
tirthas.description: This tirtha is also known as Garuda tirtha. After taking bath in the tirtha, it is customary to worship the Vaman incarnation of Lord Vishnu. This tirtha is also one of the tirtha associated with Vaman incarnation of Lord Vishnu in Kurukshetra. Folk beliefs associate this place with the birth of Ghatotkacha, the son of Bhima from Hiddimba. There is a tank to the east of the temple which has Late medieval bathing ghat made of lakhori bricks. Apart from this, medieval pottery has also been found in the tirtha premises.

tirthas.name: Bala Sundari Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Temple dedicated to the family goddess of Pandavas
tirthas.description: According to folklore, the goddess of this tirtha is the family goddess of the Pandavas, whose symbolic form was found here by a saint who came from Maharashtra in the medieval times. After finding the Pindi or symbolic form of the goddess a temple of the goddess was built at this place. The people of this region also consider this goddess as their family deity. There is also a tradition of performing the tonsure ceremony of children here. Painted Grey Ware associated with Mahabharata period and some medieval potteries have also been found from the vicinity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Baranavati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is located in the area of ancient Kamyak forest
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located in the area of ancient Kamyak forest. Local people also call it Ban tirtha. During their exile, Pandavas stayed in Kamyak forest for a long time. This village must have been named Barana because it is located on the bank of the River Varanavati. In the 17th century CE, Guru Teg Bahadur also visited the village and preached Satnaam to his followers. There are Late-medieval ghats at the tirtha. Medieval pottery has also been found from the surroundings of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Kaushiki Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The tirtha located on River Kaushiki in Aditi forest
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located on the banks of River Kaushiki, a tributary of the River Saraswati. In ancient times, this tirtha must have been located in the Aditi forest itself. Folk tradition knew this tirtha as Manasi Ganga. Apart from the ancient structures, remains of the Late medieval Ghats can also be seen here. From the mound of Abhimanyupur situated in the vicinity of this tirtha, one finds antiquities from the proto-historic period to the Late medieval period. These remains prove the antiquity of all the tirthas of this region.

tirthas.name: Amba Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is located to the west of Aditi tirtha
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located to the west of Aditi tirtha. In ancient times, Aditi forest was one of the seven major forests situated in the land of Kurukshetra. Many tirthas must have existed in this great forest. Amba tirtha is associated with Amba or mother goddess. Mother Aditi, the wife of sage Kashyapa, is considered the mother of gods. Therefore, this tirtha must have been related to Aditi or some other goddess. The mound adjacent to the tirtha contains archaeological remains from the proto-historic period to the Late medieval period.

tirthas.name: Som Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: According to folklore, Som deity, the moon god, attained health by worshipping Lord Shiva here
tirthas.description: According to folklore, Som deity, the moon god, attained health by worshipping Lord Shiva here. The villagers also call this tirtha Shasmaali. The presence of this tirtha in Aditi forest area shows the tradition of ancient planet worship. Antiquities of the proto-historic period are found in the tirtha premises, among which the images of Yaksha and Yaksha-Yakshini of the 2nd century BCE are noteworthy. Probably in the past, this tirtha must have been a part of the archaeological mound of Abhimanyupur.

tirthas.name: Saraswati Ghat
tirthas.shortDescription: Located on the bank of the River Saraswati, this tirtha is also associated with Ashtakosi Parikrama of Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: Located on the bank of the River Saraswati, this tirtha is also associated with Ashtakosi Parikrama of Kurukshetra. This parikrama starts from Nabhi Kamal tirtha and reaches this Saraswati Ghat via Kartik temple, Sthanvishwar Mahadev temple and Kuber tirtha. After this tirtha, the devotees visit Rantuk Yaksha, Shiv temple-Palwal, Ban Ganga-Dayalpur, Bhishma Kund-Narkatari and this journey ends again at Nabhi Kamal tirtha. There are two ghats with octagonal turrets of medieval period at this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Ram Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Myths relate this tirtha to Parashurama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu
tirthas.description: Myths relate this tirtha to Parashurama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu. It is said that after performing the Vajpeya yajna and one hundred Ashvamedha yajnas, he gifted the entire earth to sage Kashyap. Balarama, the elder brother of Krishna also visited this tirtha during his pilgrimage. Located on old palaeochannel of River Saraswati, this tirtha has medieval ghats. It has yielded earthen pots and remains related from ancient to medieval times.

tirthas.name: Kuber Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The place where Kubera was made treasurer of gods
tirthas.description: According to the scripture, Kuber, the king of Yakshas attained the position of treasurer of the gods, after performing severe penance here. This tirtha is located on the stream of River Saraswati. The tirtha was visited by Balarama, the elder brother of Krishna during his pilgrimage to the land of Kurukshetra. Jagatguru Sri Vallabhacharya also stayed at this tirtha, which is considered to be his 75th visiting point out of 84 tirthas hallowed by him. This tirtha site has archaeological remains from ancient to medieval times, which also proves its antiquity.

tirthas.name: Badarpachan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is associated with Arundhati, the wife of sage Vasishtha and Shrutavati, the daughter of sage Bharadwaj
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with Arundhati, the wife of sage Vasishtha and Shrutavati, the daughter of sage Bharadwaj. According to the Mahabharata, Arundhati cooked berry fruits for Shiva and Shrutavati cooked them for Indra, the king of gods. Presently, this tirtha is also known as Nand-Bhauji Tirtha. Lord Krishna's elder brother Balarama visited this tirtha before reaching to Kuber tirtha. This tirtha which is located on the bank of ancient River Saraswati, has yielded Late-medieval

tirthas.name: Sri Kaleshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Popular belief associates this tirtha with king Ravana of Lanka, who is said to have worshipped Lord Shiva here in the absence of Nandi
tirthas.description: Popular belief associates this tirtha with king Ravana of Lanka, who is said to have worshipped Lord Shiva here in the absence of Nandi. This is the only temple in India where there is no image of Nandi. According to Vaman Puran, the Linga here was established by Rudra who is capable of removing all the sins of the devotees. From the archaeological point of view, ancient remains dating from Ist to the 18th century CE are found around this place.

tirthas.name: Shukra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Shukracharya, the preceptor of demons
tirthas.description: Located on the bank of River Saraswati, this tirtha is considered to be the place of penances performed by Shukracharya, the preceptor of demons. It is said that Shukracharya had revived the dead demons by applying Mrit Sanjivani Vidya on them which he had learnt from Lord Shiva. According to Brahma Puran, this tirtha fulfills all the wishes of human beings and eradicates their all the sins and diseases. There exists a temple which has paintings on its walls and ceilings.

tirthas.name: Galav Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The seat of penances of sage Galav
tirthas.description: This tirtha is accosiated with sage Galav, the son of sage Vishwamitra. After receiving education from his father, he gave 600 horses and Madhvi, the daughter of king Yayati, as Guru Dakshina to his father Vishwamitra. This same sage Galav used to grace the assembly of Indra, the king of gods and Yudhishthira with his presence, as mentioned in Sabha Parva of Mahabharata. This sage Galav had performed severe penances for a long time at this place, due to which this pilgrimage became famous as Galav tirtha.

tirthas.name: Saptasaraswat Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Confluence place of seven Saraswati
tirthas.description: Tradition believes that seven streams of River Saraswati flowed together to fill this tirtha. According to Vaman Puran, the confluence of seven Saraswatis makes this tirtha rarerest in three worlds. This tirtha is also called the seat of penances of sage Mankanak who was a great devotee of Lord Shiva. According to popular belief, Ganga appears in a well named Gangakoop situated at the premises of tirtha on the day of Baisakhi. Bathing from the waters of this well on this occasion is considered equivalent to bathing in the Ganges.

tirthas.name: Brahma Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the largest tirthas of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: This tirtha is one of the largest tirthas of Kurukshetra region. It is said in the Mahabharata that by visiting this tirtha, a person gets the fruits of performing Rajsuya and Ashvamedha yajnas. According to scripture, a person who stays in this tirtha for three nights gets the fruits of donating thousands of cows and achieves the heaven. According to the Puranas, sage Markandeya received the Mahamrityunjaya Mantra from sage Bhrigu under a tree named Ballivat situated at the tirtha. The bricks and earthen pots of Kushana and Gupta period recovered from here prove the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Som Tirth
tirthas.shortDescription: It is said that Som Dev, suffering from the disease of tuberculosis due to the curse of Daksha Prajapati
tirthas.description: It is said that Som Dev, suffering from the disease of tuberculosis due to the curse of Daksha Prajapati. He freed himself from that terrible disease by performing fierce and rigorous penance at this place. It is said that by taking a bath in Som tirtha here, a person gets the fruits of performing Rajsuya yajna and becomes free from all diseases, sorrows and faults and he attains the world of moon god and lives there happily for a long time. The ruined pillars and sculptures of a temple of Pratihara period (9th-10th century CE) from the tirtha premises prove the antiquity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Renuka Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Renua, the mother of Parashurama
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with Renuka, the mother of Parashurama. Once, Surya, disguised as a Brahmin, had sought forgiveness from sage Jamadagni for the pain caused to Renuka by scorching heat. According to the Mahabharata if someone visits this excellent tirtha and takes bath here and worships the forefathers and gods, gets free from all sins and achieves the fruits of performing Agnishtom yajna. According to the Vamana Purana by bathing in the waters of this tirtha the seeker gets the fruit of motherly devotion.

tirthas.name: Prithudak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The tirtha par excellence in Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, tirtha located on the bank of the River Saraswati was considered as the best tirtha of the entire land of Kurukshetra. According to the Vaman Puran, Lord Shiva also took a ritualistic bath in Prithudak tirtha. It is said that a person who leaves his body while chanting at this tirtha is undoubtedly entitled to an eternal position. The archaeological remains found in the vicinity of the tirtha confirm the literary description of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Brahmayoni Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Brahma, the creator
tirthas.description: It is said that Lord Brahma made the rules of Varnashram Dharma at this tirtha standing on the bank of the River Saraswati. According to the Vaman Puran, the said tirtha was built by Brahma. It is said in the Mahabharata that a person who bathes in the Brahmayoni tirtha with a pure, restrained and sacred mind attains the world of Brahma and undoubtedly uplifts his lineage. Prithudak and Saraswati tirtha lay in the south and north of this tirtha. Bathing at this tirtha on Saturday leads to salvation.

tirthas.name: Saraswati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Prominent salvation ensuring tirtha on the bank of River Saraswati
tirthas.description: River Saraswati is considered to be a major river of Vedic period on the bank of which King Matinar chose her as his consort after performing many yajnas. It is said that Asim Krishna, a descendant of Pandavas, performed Yajnas here for 12 years on the banks of River Saraswati. Shradh and Pinddaan are performed at this tirtha for the salvation of forefathers. In the tirtha complex, an inscription of 9th century CE is found which describes the fair organized at Prithudak tirtha. The famous Kartik temple is also located in the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Prachi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha located on east ward flowing Saraswati
tirthas.description: At this tirtha of Kurukshetra region, River Saraswati flows towards the east, due to which it is famous as Prachi tirtha. According to the Puranas, nothing remains attainable for one either in this world or in other world who performs Shradha at this tirtha. Here, on the bank of River Saraswati, three temples of the Late medieval period can exist. A large number of sculptures of Pratihara period (9th-10th century CE) can be seen in one of these temples. This shows the religious and cultural importance of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Arunai Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the prominent tirtha related to Shiva
tirthas.description: The story of the origin of this tirtha is related to sages Vishwamitra and Vashishtha whose hermitages were located on the banks of River Saraswati. Seers and sages brought the River Aruna here to clean the blood-soaked River Saraswati due to Vishwamitra's curse. This confluence of River Saraswati and River Aruna became famous as Arunai tirtha. It is said that a person who stays here and bathes with restraint for three nights becomes free from all sins.

tirthas.name: Som Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Som tirthas of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to Vaman Puran, this tirtha is has been related to Som, the moon god. According to popular belief, Som, who was suffering from the curse of Daksha Prajapati and was forgiven by the kingdom, freed himself from that terrible disease by performing fierce and rigorous penance at this place situated on the bank of River Saraswati. By taking bath at this tirtha, a person obtains the fruits of performing Rajsuya Yajna and becomes free from all diseases, sorrows and defects. Besides, devotee also attains the worlds of moon god and lives there happily for a long time.

tirthas.name: Manipurak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Arjuna's marriage
tirthas.description: According to folklore, Arjuna married Chitrangada, the daughter of king Chitravahan, at this place and lived here for about three years. Folklore also relates this tirtha to Ashwatthama where the Pandavas seized the gem attached to his forehead. Remains of Late Harappan period to the medieval period are found from the bank of River Saraswati near this tirtha. This indicates the importance and antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Shalihotra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with the dialogue between Yaksha & Yudhishthira
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with sage Shalihotra. The dialogue between Yaksha and Yudhishthira took place at this place. Yudhishthira had answered all the questions of Yaksha and got back the life of his four brothers Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva from the Yaksha. According to folklore, Parashurama started his campaign against unjust kings from here after killing King Sahasrabahu. According to Mahabharata, a person gets the reward of donating a thousand cows by taking bath in the waters of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Bhurishrava Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The place of heroic death of Bhurishrava
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Bhurishrava, one of the commander of Kauravas in Mahabharata war. He had defeated the armies of Pandavas several times. During the war he also killed ten sons of Satyaki, the cousin of Krishna and commander of Pandavas. Once when Bhurishrava was about to kill Satyaki, Arjun pierced his right arm with an arrow. Immediately Satyaki killed Bhurishrava when he was grieved and sitting in meditation. Being a devotee of Lord Shiva, the temple situated at the tirtha is called Bhurishraveshwar Mahadev.

tirthas.name: Lomash Tirth
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha situated in the ancient Kamyak forest is considered to be the place of penance of sage Lomash
tirthas.description: This tirtha situated in the ancient Kamyak forest is considered to be the place of penance of sage Lomash. He was a great storyteller. He narrated the message of Indra and Arjuna to Yudhishthira in Kamyak forest and apprised the Pandavas about their well-being and the attainment of divine weapons by Arjuna. Sage Lomash narrated the tales of sage Agastya, Rama, Parshurama, Sage Dadhichi's great sacrifice and also the story of King Sagar, the descent of Ganga on earth by Bhagirath etc. to Yudhishthira. These stories occur in Mahabharata epic.

tirthas.name: Kamyak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the seven forests of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located on the bank of River Saraswati in the ancient Kamyak forest of Kurukshetra where the Pandavas met Ved Vyas during their exile. Lord Krishna, Vidur and sage Maitreya also came to see the Pandavas here. The Pandavas also met sage Markandeya in this forest. Draupadi was also kidnapped by Jayadrath in this forest. According to folklore, Ashwatthama, who is believed to be immortal, performs one sandhya puja out of three Sandhyas here at this tirtha. A fair is held at this tirtha when Shukla Saptami falls on Sunday.

tirthas.name: Karna Ka Tila
tirthas.shortDescription: A famous archaeological site of Kurukhsetra
tirthas.description: Folklore associate this mound with Karna, one of the prominent warrior of Kaurava side during Mahabharata war. According to popular belief, Karna used to operate in Mahabharata war from this place. This mound was first surveyed by A. Cunningham and excavated by D.B. Spooner. The excavation conducted by Kurukshetra University have yielded archaeological remains from 400 BC to 18th century CE. These include Painted Grey Ware, red shiny and black polished potteries, stone beads, figures of animals, seals with Brahmi inscriptions etc. Remains of medieval settlements have also been found from here at the top level.

tirthas.name: Aapga Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The salvation ensuring tirtha located on the bank of River Aapga
tirthas.description: The Vaman Puran mentions nine rivers located in the land of Kurukshetra. Out of these nine rivers, accepts River Saraswati all were seasonal rivers. This tirtha is situated on one of these rivers named as River Aapga which followed between saraswati and Drishadvati as mentioned in the Rigveda. According to the Puranas, a person who offers Pind Daan at this tirtha in the month of Bhadrapad, especially on the Chaturdashi of Krishna Paksha at noon, attains salvation. Remains of the Late-Harappan culture have been found from Mirzapur mound near the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Ojas Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Kartikeya, the son of Shiva
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with Kumar Kartikeya, the son of Lord Shiva. According to the Mahabharata, the gods conferred the post of commander of their army on Kumar Kartikeya and anointed him at this tirtha situated on the bank of River Saraswati. According to the VamanPurana, the place where Kumar was anointed is famous by the name Ojas. By taking bath in the waters of this tirtha, a person attains fame and a person who performs Shraddha here attains the world of Kumar Kartikey. The Shraddha performed here is considered immortal.

tirthas.name: Kulottaraan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha has been named Kulottaraan as it gives salvation to the generations of the devouts
tirthas.description: This tirtha has been named Kulottaraan as it gives salvation to the generations of the devouts. According to Vaman Puran, this tirtha was created by Lord Vishnu himself. By taking bath in the waters of this tirtha a persons saves his 21 generations. According to tradition, Yudhishthira performed Shraddha and Pinddaan for the peace of the souls of the warriors killed in the Mahabharata war at this tirtha. Ghats and temples of Late medieval period exist at this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Tripurari Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is associated with the destruction of Tripuras, the three cities of demons by Lord Shiva
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with the destruction of Tripuras, the three cities of demons by Lord Shiva. It is said that the demon Maya built three cities made of gold, silver and iron for three sons of demon Tarakasur known as Varakaksha, Kamalakaksha, Vidyutmali. All these three cities were destroyed by Lord Shiva with a single arrow on the request of the gods. For this reason, Lord Shiva was named Tripurari. Folklore connects this incident with this tirtha of Kurukshetra. Lord Shiva pleases quickly after being worshipped here by the devotees.

tirthas.name: Aditi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is situated in the Aditi forest area of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: This tirtha is situated in the Aditi forest area of ancient Kurukshetra. According to the VamanPurana, a woman who bathes in the waters of this tirtha and sees Aditi is freed from all sins and gives birth to a brave son. It is said that at this place Aditi, the mother of gods, performed severe penances for thousands of years and conceived Martand (Aditya) as her son. According to folklore, Abhimanyu attained martyrdom while breaking the Chakravyuh at this place. There is a huge archaeological mound to the west of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Birthplace of the Gita
tirthas.shortDescription: Witness of first day battle of Mahabharata war
tirthas.description: It is believed that Lord Krishna preached the Gita to Arjuna at this place before the commencement of Mahabharata war. It is said that Adi Guru Shankaracharya was first to have marked this place during his journey to Himalayas. In 1850, king of Kashmir built a temple here. After this, in 1924, king of Darbhanga built a platform around the Banyan tree, which is believed to have witnessed the delivery of message of Bhagavadgita. The fragment of a temple pillar of 9th-10th century kept in the platform built around the banyan tree also reveals the historical importance of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Bhishma Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: According to popular legends, Bhishma, the commander in chief of Kauravas lay on a bed of arrows on the 10th day of Mahabharata war
tirthas.description: According to popular legends, Bhishma, the commander in chief of Kauravas lay on a bed of arrows on the 10th day of Mahabharata war after being injured by Arjuna's arrows. He breathed his last only after the sun entered into the northern hemisphere. After Mahabharata war, it was here that Yudhishthira learnt the teachings of Rajdharma- the statecraft and discipline from Bhishma. Before his death, Bhishma also praised Lord Krishna reciting Vishnu Sahasranama. It is a major tirtha of Ashtakoshi Parikrama of Kurukshetra.

tirthas.name: Baan Ganga
tirthas.shortDescription: Many folk tales are popular about the origin of this tirtha
tirthas.description: Many folk tales are popular about the origin of this tirtha. According to one legend, before killing Jayadratha on 14th day of the Mahabharata war, Arjuna shot an arrow called Parjanyastra at this place and created a stream of water. Krishna had bathed the tired horses of Arjuna's chariot with the water that came out of this stream. For this reason this tirtha is called Baan Ganga. A bow like structure made of Lakhori bricks has been built in the tank of the tirtha. Some Late medieval temples are also standing in the tirthas premises.

tirthas.name: Brahma Sarovar
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is associated with Lord Brahma
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with Lord Brahma. According to folklore, this tank was first renovated by king Kuru, the ancestor of Kauravas and Pandavas. Bathing in this tank on the occasion of solar eclipse is considered to be equivalent to the fruits of performing thousands of Ashvamedha yajnas. Remains of an ancient Buddhist stupa, structures and archaeological remains of early historic period have been found on the western bank of this tank, which prove the antiquity of this sacred tank.

tirthas.name: Sannihit Sarovar
tirthas.shortDescription: According to the Puranas, on the occasion of Amavasya, all waters of all the trithas located on the earth gather here
tirthas.description: According to the Puranas, on the occasion of Amavasya, all waters of all the trithas located on the earth gather here. For this reason this tirtha has been named as Sannihit. There is an ancient tradition of offering pind-daan and shraddha for forefathers here at this tirtha. According to the Bhagavata Puran, during a total solar eclipse, Krishna who had come here from Dwarka and met Nanda, Yashoda and other cow-herds who had come here from the region of Gokul and Vrindavan (Mathura).

tirthas.name: Nabhi Kamal Tirth
tirthas.shortDescription: It is said that at this place, while Lord Vishnu was resting in Kshirsagar, a lotus flower emerged from his navel which gave birth to Brahma
tirthas.description: It is said that at this place, while Lord Vishnu was resting in Kshirsagar, a lotus flower emerged from his navel which gave birth to Brahma, the creator. Brahma started the creation of the universe here on the orders of Lord Vishnu. On the occasion of Krishna Chaturdashi falling in the month of Chaitra, the famous Ashtakosi Parikrama of Kurukshetra starts from here and also concluded here. To the north of the tirtha lies a famous archaeological site called Raja Harsha Ka Tila.

tirthas.name: Sthaneshwar Mahadev Mandir
tirthas.shortDescription: It is said that Lord Brahma himself had established the Sthanu Linga of Lord Shiva here
tirthas.description: It is said that Lord Brahma himself had established the Sthanu Linga of Lord Shiva here, In the Vaman Puran, apart from many tirthas around Sthanu tirtha, there is also a mention of a large Banyan tree to the north, east, south and west are the abodes of the deities like Shukra, Som, Daksh and Skanda respectively. The present Thanesar city was named after Sthanu tirtha, which was called Sthanvishvara in ancient times. Before Mahabharata war, Pandavas had pleased Lord Shiva at this site and received the boon of victory in the forthcoming war.

tirthas.name: Maa Bhadrakali Mandir
tirthas.shortDescription: According to the Mahabharata, the holy land of Kurukshetra is situated between the River Saraswati and Drishadvati
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, the holy land of Kurukshetra is situated between the River Saraswati and Drishadvati. Four Yakshas are located in the four cardinal corners of this land. In Mahabharata, these Yakshas have been named as Tarantuka, Arantuka, Ramhrada and Machkruka. This tirtha dedicated to Rantuk Yaksha is located on the bank of River Saraswati at a place called Bir Pipli in Kurukshetra. According to scriptures, pilgrims should visit this land only after seeing the Yakshas. This tirtha is also presently known as Chitta Temple.

tirthas.name: Brihaspati Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the kunds dedicated to the nine planets
tirthas.description: This Graha Kund is dedicated to Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods. It was also built by Yudhishthira, which is located in the northern direction of Surya Kund. There is a Late medieval temple dedicated to Brihaspati and Lord Shiva at the tirtha, the interior of which has some wall paintings. The Tirtha tank lies to the east of the temple complex, has Late medieval male and female bathing ghats with octagonal turrets. Earlier, there was a tradition of taking bath at this tirtha during the month of Kartik every year.

tirthas.name: Aapga Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated on the ancient River Aapaga
tirthas.description: Aapga, the holy river of Rigvedic period is also mentioned in the Mahabharata and the Vaman Puran. This river was a major tributary of River Saraswati. According to the Mahabharata, a person who bathes here, worships the divinities and ancestors and stays here for one night, gets the fruits of performing Agnishtom Yajna. The Vaman Puran states that a person who offers Pind Daan here in the afternoon of Chaturdashi of Krishna Paksha of the month Bhadrapad, attains salvation.

tirthas.name: Shuddhaspada Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Mahabharata war
tirthas.description: A reference of the tirtha is found in the Vana Parva of Mahabharata where it is mentioned after Rudrakoti Tirtha. According to local belief, water was supplied to the armies from here during the Mahabharata war. Out of the seven wells of ancient times, only three wells are seen here now. In the past, the water of this tirtha was considered as pure and clean as the water of River Ganga. In Late medieval times, there was a hermitage of the famous saint Baba Dayalpuri, whose samadhi-temple stands along with the Shiva temple in the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Sarvroghar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Disease curing tirtha of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: According to folklore, king Janmejaya, the son of Parikshit got relief from a serious skin disease here. The tank here is famous by the name of Siddh Johri whose water is still considered miraculous for skin diseases. It is said that during the Mahabharata war, the injured warriors as well as the wounded animals used to be cured by its waters. The Samadhi temple of Baba Devi Das situated at the tirtha is indicative of a long ascetic tradition. The archaeological remains from the Late Harappan to the Early historical period from the vicinity of the tirtha show the antiquity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Kulottaraan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the salvation ensuring tirtha of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: The tirtha named Kulottaraan is mentioned in the the Mahabharata and Vaman Puran, which ensures salvation in the Kurukshetra region. Village Kultaran is named after this tirtha. According to folklore, the Pandavas performed Tarpan and Pind-daan for their ancestors at this tirtha. Since then, the tradition of offering Pind-daan and Tarpan is continuing here on every Amavasya. The temples of Shiva, Hanuman and Samadhi temples of saints exist at this tirtha. Of these main Samadhi temple belongs to Baba Balwan Giri.

tirthas.name: Niraakar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to Lord Shiva
tirthas.description: This tirtha is named after Niraakar, one of the names of Lord Shiva. According to popular belief, women used to take bath here during the Mahabharata war. Late medieval ghats with chambers exist on the tirtha tank. The pottery of same period have been found in the tirtha complex. At a distance of one kilometer archaeological remains from the Late Harappan to Early historical period are also found. All these evidences indicate the cultural continuity. Earlier there was a tradition of taking bath in tirtha tank in the months of Shravan and Kartik.

tirthas.name: Dwadasha Rashi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated on the bank of River Kaushiki
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located on the palaeochannel of ancient River Kaushiki, a tributary of River Saraswati. In the Vaman Puran, Kaushiki has been called Papanashini or the destroyer of sins. From tirtha complex archaeological remains from Late Harappan period to the medieval period are found. The temple situated at the tirtha is related with some unknown Brahmachari which was built here by the king of Kashmir. There is a tradition of taking twelve dips in the tirtha tank in the name of twelve zodiac signs.

tirthas.name: Kanva Rishi Ashram
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to sage Kanva
tirthas.description: Legends relate this tirtha to sage Kanva who was the foster father of Shakuntala, the mother of king Bharat. At present, a magnificent Rama temple with Nagar Shikhara stands at the tirtha. The tirtha is located on the palaeochannel of River Drishadvati. Late medieval bathing ghats with octagonal turrets adorn the tirtha tank. Remains of structures from the Maurya period (4th century BCE) have been located in the tirtha complex. The mound, spread over about 20 acres of land near the tirtha complex, has yielded potteries and other artefacts belonging to the Harappan and Painted Grey Ware periods.

tirthas.name: Kavya Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Situated at the central point of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: This tirtha is considered to be located almost in the centre of 48 Kos Kurukshetra region. So, the local people count this tirtha among the most special tirthas of Kurukshetra. According to popular legends, Brahma had performed yajya at this place. According to popular belief, if Ekadashi of month of Magh falls on Sunday, then taking bath here gives the merit of performing crores of yajnas. Three temples are standing in the tirtha complex, of these one was built in Late medieval times while two other modern contructions.

tirthas.name: Veer Barbarik Shyam Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to the Mahabharata
tirthas.description: According to folklore, before the Mahabharata war, Lord Krishna had asked for the head of Ghatotkach's son Barbarik in donation here. After that his head was kept on a pillar in the nearby village Serhada from where Barbarik watched the entire Mahabharata war for eighteen days. The tirtha tank has Late medieval ghats with octagonal turrets. From the western bank of the tirtha tank remains of structures of 8th-9th century CE and structures of Kushan period of 1st-2nd century CE have been found. Some fragments of sculptures of 9th-10th century CE are placed in the sanctum-sanctorum of the temple of Barbarik.

tirthas.name: Shani Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the kunds dedicated to the nine planets
tirthas.description: This kund is located to the north-western direction of Surya Kund, which was also built by Yudhishthira. This tirtha is also called Diwal Wala. There are two Late medieval temples dedicated to Lord Shani and Lord Shiva at the tirtha, Tirtha tank is situated to the north-west of the temple with Late medieval ghats with octagonal turrets which have been renovated recently. Bricks of 8th-9th century CE have also been found from the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Shukra Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Kunds dedicated to the nine planets
tirthas.description: This kund was also built by Yudhishthira, which is situated towards the south-east of Surya Kund. Pataleshwar Mahadev temple of Nagar style situated at the tirtha is a temple of the Late medieval period, which is important from the point of view of architecture. Bricks of 8th-9th century CE have been found from the tirtha complex. The credit for the renovation of this tirtha goes to Seth Chhajjumal, the minister of Bhai Uday Singh, the ruler of Kaithal. Because of this association, the tirtha is also called Chhajju Kund.

tirthas.name: Budh Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Kunds dedicated to the nine planets
tirthas.description: Along with other nine Grah Kunds, this Kund was also constructed by Yudhishthira on the advice of Lord Krishna. Among the Kunds dedicated to the nine planets, this Kund dedicated to Budh or planet Mercury is located to the east of the main Surya Kund. A Late medieval temple with Nagar Shikhara is dedicated to Budh and Lord Shiva stands at the tirtha. Shivalinga is installed here with the human image of Budh. The rectangular tank located near the temple has stairs built from all four sides. Bathing here on Shravan Trayodashi has special significance.

tirthas.name: Surya Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the kunds dedicated to the nine planets
tirthas.description: According to folklore, Yudhishthira, who was upset by the massacre of many heroes in the Mahabharata war, had constructed sacred Kunds dedicated to the nine planets in the land of Kurukshetra on the advice of Lord Krishna. Out of these nine Kundas, this Kund is know as Surya Kund. The other eight Kunds related to the planets of Kaithal town were built in the four cardinal directions of Surya Kund. Kaithal town is also called Choti Kashi due to its association with the nine planets. Late medieval bathing ghats with octagonal towers have been built at this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Sarak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: A rare Rudra tirtha of Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, crores of tirthas are present at this tirtha. By seeing Lord Shiva at this tirtha on the Chaturdashi of Krishna paksha, all the wishes of a person are fulfilled and he attains heaven. Here Rudrakoti is situated in the well in the middle of the tank of the tirtha. A person who takes bath and remembers Rudrakoti, undoubtedly worships Rudrakoti and by the blessings of Rudras, he gets freed from all sins and attains the ultimate aim of life.

tirthas.name: Dharmakund
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to Yama
tirthas.description: According to local belief, this tirtha is dedicated to Yama, the god of truth or Dharma. At this tirtha the sacred bath is allowed only for local people. The pilgrims coming from outside are prohibited to take bath in the waters of this tirtha. They can only worship at this tirtha. Medieval potteries and lakhori bricks are found in the tirtha premises. However, potteries and other antiquities of Early historic period are found in the vicinity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Balakhilya Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The seat of penance of sages Balakhilyas
tirthas.description: According to the Vaman Puran, this tirthas is the seat of penance of sages Balakhilyas who were born from Lord Brahma at the time of the beginning of the creation. According to local beliefs, this tirtha is also known as Shobhani Rishi tirtha who might have been the mythical sage Shobhari. To the north of the tirtha, at a distance of 2 km from village Balu, there is a mound of Harappan period, from where the remains of three cultures i.e. Pre-Harappan, Mature-Harappan and Late-Harappan period have been excavated.

tirthas.name: Amarhrad Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha which ensures immortality
tirthas.description: Local belief associates this tirtha with king Dang of Mahabharata period, due to which it is also called as Dangali tirtha. In the Mahabharata, it has been called Amarhrad tirtha, according to which, by worshipping Indra after taking bath in the waters of this tirtha, one gets immortality. Remains from the Late Harappan period to the medieval period are found from the vicinity of the tirtha. An image of goddess Amba dating 7th-8th century CE recovered near this site is displayed in Srikrishna Museum, Kurukshetra.

tirthas.name: Sritirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to goddess Lakshmi
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, a devotee with a restrained heart attains abundant wealth and prosperity after taking bath in the waters of this tirtha. The Narada Purana states that a devotee who bathes in the waters of this tirtha and worships Lord Vishnu always feels the presence of deity with him. Bricks of the early medieval period and a stone female head dating 7th-8th century CE have been found from here. The surroundings of the tirtha contain archaeological remains from Late Harappan period to the Early historic times.

tirthas.name: Jadbharat Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Bharat, son of king Rishabhdev
tirthas.description: This tirtha is one of the largest tirthas of 48 Kos Kurukshetra region. Popular belief associates this tirtha with Bharat, son of king Rishabhdev of solar dynasty of Ayodhya. Bharat was born as a deer in his second birth. It is believed that by taking bath at this tank and worshipping Lord Vishnu, one attains self-knowledge. The ghats of the tirtha are built of medieval lakhori bricks. Some broken sculptures and potteries belonging to 9th-10th century CE have been found from the tirtha premises.

tirthas.name: Vindusar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to Goddess Vindeshwari
tirthas.description: According to folklore, before the Mahabharata war, the Pandavas worshipped Goddess Vindeshwari at this site. Local legends consider this tirtha to be an hermitage of sage Kardam, whose second hermitage is located in the nearby village named Barot. The tirtha complex has the samadhis of many sages and saints. A late medieval temple located in the Tirtha complex has wall paintings. A Late medieval ghat made of lakhori bricks also exist at the tank of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Jamdagni Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to sage Jamdagni
tirthas.description: According to folklore, Jamdagni, the great grandson of sage Orva and son of Richik, stayed at this tirtha during his pilgrimage. Sage Jamdagni, born in the Bhrigu clan, was the father of sage Parashurama. There are samadhis of many saints in the tirtha complex. For this reason, the tradition of Rishi Puja has been going on here since the distant past. Late medieval ghats with octagonal turrets made of lakhori bricks exist at the tank of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Chyavan Rishi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The place of penance of sage Chyavan
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to sage Chyavan who was given youthfulness by Ashwini Kumars, the physicians of the gods. In return for this favour, sage Chyavan made them eligible to drink Somras. According to folklore, during the Mahabharata war, food was prepared here for the Pandavas and their camp. Therefore, in folk belief, it is also called Chulha tirtha. Early historic and medieval artefacts have been found from the vicinity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Panchtirthi
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to five deities of Sanatan Dharma
tirthas.description: This tirtha, popularly known as Panchtirthi, is situated on the border of five villages named Sangroli, Sakra, Dherdu, Kaul and Kheri Sakra. In the past, there might have been temples or places of worship of all five sub-sects of Hinduism related to five major deities i.e. Shiva, Surya, Vishnu, Ganesha and Shakti. This tirtha is also known as Sadhu Wala Dera. There is a Late medieval well in the tirtha complex. The medieval pottery and other archaeological remains found from the tirtha complex prove its antiquity.

tirthas.name: Khatvangeshwar Tirth
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the major Shaivite tirthas of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with king Khandeshwar of Ayodhya who rested and prayed Lord Shiva here. King Khandeshwar had settled a village named Khadalwa at this place but the village at present is not into existence. The temple of the tirtha has a huge stone Shivlinga. The height of this Shivlinga is about two feet. Bricks and potteries dating first century CE have been found from the tirtha complex, which proves the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Mukuteshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with sage Markandeya
tirthas.description: Popular legend relates this tirtha to sage Markandeya, who was born at this place. The name of sage Markandeya and Markandeya tirtha occurs in various Puranas. It is said that at this tirtha, Lord Shiva had killed Yama to protect sage Markandeya and had revived Yama's life again on the request of the divinities. Late medieval ghats can be seen in the tank of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Kapilmuni Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tritha associated with sage Kapil, the exponent of Sankhya system of philosophy
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to the conversation held between sage Kapil and his mother Devahuti. According to the Mahabharata, a person who observes celibacy and worships the divinities and ancestors with a reverential mind after bathing in Kapil tirtha, gets the fruits of donating a thousand of cows. It is said in the Vaman Puran that a person who sees Shiva at this tirtha is entitled to salvation. Two brick temples of 7th century CE are at tirtha complex, which are among the rare brick temples of India.

tirthas.name: Manush Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Higher birth providing tirtha
tirthas.description: The earliest mention of the Manush tirtha occurs in the Rigveda where kings of the Bharat clan had performed yajnas. It shows the antiquity of the site. According to Mahabharata the deers injured by the hunter's arrow got human body after bathing in this tank, hence this tirtha was named as Manush tirtha. The Vaman Puran and the Skanda Purana also describe the origin of this tirtha as it has been described in the Mahabharata. A person attains salvation just by hearing about this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Brahmodumbar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Brahma
tirthas.description: This is one of the tirthas related to Lord Brahma in Kurukshetra region. At the tirtha were present seven sacred ponds dedicated to seven great sages Bhardwaj, Gautam, Jamadagni, Kashyap, Vishwamitra, Vashishtha and Atri. According to the Mahabharata, by taking bath in the ponds dedicated to seven great sage, a person attains the world of Brahma. In the Vaman Puran, this tirtha has been called Brahmodumbar because it is associated with Lord Brahma. The artefacts of Kushan period (Ist century CE) from the mound adjacent to the tirtha tank prove the antiquity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Suryakund
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to Surya, the Sun god
tirthas.description: This tirtha is one of the Suryakund located in Surya van, one of the seven forests situated in ancient Kurukshetra region. Since time immemorial the land of Kurukshetra has been famous for its solar worship. Many water bodies of this reason are called Surya Kunds where the devotees come to take sacred bath on the occasion of Amavasya in general and solar eclipse in particular. The walls of a Late medieval temple are profusely painted with floral ornamentation.

tirthas.name: Gobhavan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha providing the fruits of making donation of cows
tirthas.description: This Tirtha is mentioned by the name of Gavan Bhavan in the Mahabharata and the Padma Purana. According to the Mahabharata, the devotee should go to Gavan Bhavan tirtha and take sacred bath there. The person doing this act gets the fruits of donating a thousand of cows. According to popular folklore, an ascetic named Nyalgiri had made a dead cow to take bath in the tank of the tirtha due to which it was revived. It is considered best to take bath at this tirtha on sixth day of Shukla Paksha of the month of Bhadrapad.

tirthas.name: Shringi Rishi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to sage Shringi and goddess Shankhini
tirthas.description: This tirtha is mentioned in the Mahabharata which is associated with sage Shringi and goddess Shankhini, It is said that a person devoted to this tirtha attains the best form by taking sacred bath in the waters of this tirtha. Goddess Shankhini is named as Sangini in the Vaman Puran. According to popular belief, Goddess Shankhini worshipped sage Shringi at this tirtha and did penance at Behar Jakh. The walls of the existing temple have paintings of Matsya Avatar and Raaslila.

tirthas.name: Arantuk Yaksha
tirthas.shortDescription: The place of Yaksha situated on the north-west corner of Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: Arantuk Yaksha of the north-west corner was situated on the bank of River Saraswati. According to the Mahabharata, a person gets the fruit of performing Agnishtom yajna by taking bath here. A medieval sculpture of Lord Vishnu depicting incarnations have been recovered from this tirtha. To the south-east of this tirha lies a Gurudwara dedicated to Guru Teg Bahadur, the ninth Guru of the Sikhs.

tirthas.name: Brahmavarta Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Brahma
tirthas.description: Situated on the border of 48 Kos Kurukshetra region, this is one of the tirthas related to Lord Brahma. According to the Mahabharata, a person attains the world of Lord Brahma by taking sacred bath in the waters of this tirtha. It is said in the Vamana Purana that a person becomes an expert in Brahmavidya by taking bath in this tirtha. Such person can give up his life according to his wish. Similar importance of this tirtha is also described in the Narada Puran.

tirthas.name: Gandharva Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Gandharva
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with divine dancers known as Gandharvas. It is mentioned in the Shalya Parva of the Mahabharata that Balarama, the elder brother of Krishna, after taking bath in the waters of this tritha satisfied the Brahmins by making donations of wealth, gold and silver to them. This tirtha was existed on the bank of River Saraswati where many Gandharvas like Vishwavasu used to organize dances. Considering the importance of this tirtha, Balarama must have visited it during his pilgrimage.

tirthas.name: Ikshumati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated on the bank of River Saraswati
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located on the bank of River Saraswati also known as Ikshumati in the past. River Ikshumati has also been mentioned by Panini, in his famous grammar treatise Ashtadhyayi. In the Ayodhya Kand of the Ramayana by sage Valmiki, this river finds mention when the messengers were going to the country of Kekaya to bring prince Bharata back to Ayodhya. The remains of Early historic to medieval period have been found from an ancient mound adjacent to the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Sutirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with the world of ancestors
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, one should go to the Sutirtha where the ancestors and gods are always present. After visiting there, one should worship and anoint the ancestors and deities. The person doing this act gets the fruits of performing Ashwamedha Yajna and ultimately attains the world of ancestors. The bathing ghat at the tirtha tank is made of Late medieval Lakhori bricks. There are two Late medieval temples at the tirtha which have been renovated recently.

tirthas.name: Swargdwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated in the ancient Sheetvan
tirthas.description: It is said in the Vamana Purana that a person who takes a balanced diet and has controlled his senses must visit Sheet Van, one of the seven forests of ancient Kurukshetra. Popular tradition associates this tirtha with Sita, the daughter of king Janak. According to popular belief, Sita had entered into the earth at this place. For this reason, this tirtha is also known as Swargdwar. According to the Narada Purana, if someone takes sacred bath in the waters of this tirtha on the day of Chaturdashi of month of Chaitra, gets salvation.

tirthas.name: Matri Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Mother Goddesses
tirthas.description: According to myths, Matrikas or Mother Goddesses were born here due to the sweat droplets falling from Lord Shiva's forehead. Matrikas further destroyed the demons. On this, the gods gave the boon to mothers to be worshipped and respected like Lord Shiva. All places related to Mother Goddesses turned into the Matri tirthas. According to Brahma Puran, a person who listens, meditates and reads about Mother Goddesses attains happiness and lives long. According to the Vaman Puran, a person who takes bath here in the tirtha becomes the owner of abundant wealth.

tirthas.name: Shrikunj Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated on the bank of River Saraswati
tirthas.description: In the Mahabharata and Vamana Purana, this tirtha is said to be located on the bank of River Saraswati. According to the Mahabharata, a person gets the fruits of performing Agnishtom Yajna by taking a sacred bath here. Even in the times of the Vamana Purana, the importance of this tirtha was exactly the same as it was in the times of the Mahabharata. This tirtha is located in the forest of Seonsar in Pehowa. The bricks of early historic period recovered from here prove the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Naimish Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha established by the sages
tirthas.description: According to the Vana Parva of Mahabharata, this tirtha was built in the land of Kurukshetra by the sages living originally at Naimisharanya. According to the Mahabharata, Naimish tirtha is a holy tirtha served by the Siddhas where Brahma resides with the divinities. It is also stated that half of the sins of a person are destroyed the moment one enters to this tirtha. There are Late medieval ghats which adorn the tirtha tank. The walls of the temple are decorated with beautiful paintings.

tirthas.name: Vedvati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha existed during the times of Ramayana
tirthas.description: This tirtha of Kurukshetra region is mentioned in the Uttara Kanda of the Ramayana and in the Vamana Purana. It is said that at this tirtha, being saddened by the insult of Ravana, Vedvati entered into the fire and in the next birth was born as Sita in the house of king Janaka of Magadh. According to the Vamana Purana, by taking sacred bath here, a pilgrim gets the fruits of performing Kanya Yajna, gets rid of all sins, and attains the supreme position. According to the Mahabharata, by taking bath in this tirtha, one gets the merits of performing Agnishtom Yajna.

tirthas.name: Kotikoot Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Kunti
tirthas.description: According to the Brahma Puran, in this tirtha the waters of crores of sacred tirthas is mingled. According to popular belief, during the Mahabharata period, when Kunti was filled with remorse, then a sage advised her to take bath in one crore tirthas as a way of atonement. Then Kunti took bath here and got rid of her sins. People believe that by taking bath in the waters of this tirtha, a pilgrim is freed from all sins. Painted Grey Ware associated with Mahabharata period has been found from the surroundings of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Banteshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The seat of penance of sage Kardama
tirthas.description: According to popular belief, sage Kardam along with his wife performed severe penance here to please Lord Vishnu with a desire to get a son. Hence, it is believed that whoever takes bath in this tirtha with the desire of getting a son, definitely his boon is fulfilled. Another popular belief connects this tirtha with sage Vasishtha. The existence of Pre-medieval remains found near the tirtha tank prove the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Pavanhrad Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Pawan, the wind deity
tirthas.description: In the Mahabharata, it has been related to the Wind deity and in the Vamana Purana, it has been related to both Shiva and Wind deity. According to myths, this is the same tank where the Wind deity had disappeared after being saddened by the loss of his son and later he reappeared after being pleased by prayers sung by all the divine beings along with Brahma. Late medieval ghats have been built at the tirtha. Banke Bihari temple located here has beautiful wall paintings.

tirthas.name: Garh Ratheshyar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirthas associated with killing of Karna
tirthas.description: According to folklore, at this place, while fighting with Arjuna on the 17th day of Mahabharata war, the wheel of the chariot of Karna, the commander of Kauravas got stuck in the ground. Due to this reason, Karna was killed by the mighty Arjuna. According to popular legends, it was at this place that the Karna, the great donor presented his gold-plated tooth to Krishna who appeared before him as a Brahmin in disguise.

tirthas.name: Kulottaran Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The salvation ensuring tirtha of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: This is another Moksha tirthas of Kurukshetra region. In the Mahabharata, the name of this tirtha occurs as Kulampun. According to the Vamana Purana, this tirtha was built by Lord Vishnu to save the people who follow Varnashram Dharma. People who desire salvation visit this tirtha and get the ultimate aim of life. According to the Narada Purana, a man who visits this tirtha and takes a sacred bath here, saves his clan and lives in heaven for a Kalpa.

tirthas.name: Kapilmuni Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirthas related to sage Kapila
tirthas.description: This is one of the tirthas of Kurukshetra region related to sage Kapila, the exponent of Samkhya system of philosophy. In the tirtha complex, there is a Late medieval temple dedicated to Krishna. The paintings depict various theme such as figures of Lord Jagannath, Daan Leela, Gajalakshmi, Bhishma lying on bed of arrows, Radha Krishna, Krishna killing Kamsa, Krishna decorating Radha's braid, Narasimha, Varaha, Parshurama killing king Sahasrabahu etc. Floral ornamentation on the walls of the sanctum sanctorum of the temple have been executed carefully.

tirthas.name: Alepaak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Shaivite tirthas of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: According to the Vamana Purana, a person who worships Lord Shiva after taking sacred bath in the waters of this tirtha on Chaturdashi of Shukla Paksha in the month of Chaitra and is not even touched by sins. The Narada Purana also relates this tirtha to Lord Shiva and gives the special importance for taking bath in it on Chaturdashi of Shukla Paksha in the month of Chaitra. According to this Purana, it makes a person free from all sins. There are Late medieval ghats made of Lakhori bricks which adorned this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Dhruv Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with devotee Dhruva
tirthas.description: This tirtha related to Dhruva, the great devotee of Lord Vishnu, is mentioned in the Varaha Purana. There are ample details available about Dhruva's life and character in the Puranas, especially the Vishnu Purana. According to popular belief, Dhruva had performed severe penance by staying at this place, due to which this tirtha became famous as Dhruva Kund. It is also believed that, the gods grant the desired boon to the person who worships on the occasion of the Shukla Paksha in the month of Chaitra.

tirthas.name: Pawaneshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Dedicated to Hanuman located in Phalkivan
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located in the Phalki forest of ancient Kurukshetra. Being associated to Hanuman, the son of Pawan, this tirtha is known as Pawaneshwar tirtha. This tirtha is mentioned as Panikhaat in the Mahabharata after Phalgu tirtha. Although this pilgrimage was built later, yet the common people attach immense faith and devotion for this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Phalgu Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: A salvation providing tirtha in Phalkivan
tirthas.description: This salvation providing tirtha is situated in Phalkivan, one of the seven forests of ancient Kurukshetra region. It is considered to be the place of penance of sage Phalgu. According to the Vamana Purana, the Shraddha performed at this tirtha on Amavasya falling on Monday satisfies the ancestors and is equivalent to Shraddha performed at Gaya. On the day of Somvati Amavasya which occurs in the month of Ashwin, lakhs of pilgrims come here to perform Pind Daan to satisfy and please their ancestors. On this day Shraddha ceremony is not performed at Gaya, the famous tirtha in Bihar.

tirthas.name: Yagyasang Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirthas related to Ganga and Bhishma
tirthas.description: The popular folklore about this tirtha relates it to the Mahabharata period. It is said that Ganga and her son Gangeya (Bhishma Pitamah) performed many yajnas at this place during the Mahabharata war. Since this shrine was a place of sacrifice, it was named Yagyasang tirtha and due to its association with Gangeya, the village might have been named Gangeya at that time, which later got corrupted and became famous as Geong.

tirthas.name: Luv-Kush Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha existed during the times of Ramayana
tirthas.description: According to popular legends, it was at this place that Lava and Kusha, the sons of Lord Rama and Sita, had memorized the entire story of the Ramayana from sage Valmiki. According to popular belief, after Lava and Kusha memorized the entire Ramayana, sage Valmiki took a vow of silence. The sanctum sanctorum of the temple contains paintings. Excavation of the tirtha has yielded archaeological remains from the Ist to the 9th-10th century CE. Some earthen pots and a well of Kushana period (Ist cent. CE) existed at this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Trivishtap Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha located on the bank of ancient River Vaitarni
tirthas.description: In the Mahabharata and Vaman Puran, this tirtha is said to be situated on the bank of River Vaitarni, which is one of the nine rivers of ancient Kurukshetra, namely Saraswati, Drishadvati, Ganga, Mandakini, Madhusrava, Vasunadi, Kaushiki and Hiranyavati. This tirtha is mentioned in the Mahabharata after Pundarik tirtha. According to the Mahabharata, worshiping Lord Shiva after taking sacred bath in River Vaitarni, a person is freed from all sins and attains salvation.

tirthas.name: Devi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Devi Tirtha situated in ancient Madhuvan
tirthas.description: This Devi tirtha is situated in Madhuvan, one of the seven forests of ancient Kurukshetra region. According to the Mahabharata, one who goes to the Devi tirtha of Madhuvati with a pure heart and bathes there and worships the deities and ancestors, by the grace of the goddess he gets the merit of donating thousand cows. It is said in Vaman Puran that a person who worships the deities and ancestors here, by the grace of the goddess, gets the desired success.

tirthas.name: Pundarik Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Pundarik Yajna
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, by taking sacred bath in this tirtha, a person gets the fruit of performing Pundarik Yajna. The Vaman Puran also prescribes that this tirtha should be visited on 10th day of Shukla Paksha in the month of Chaitra. By bathing, chanting and performing shraddha at this tirtha one gets salvation. There are many Late medieval temples built at this tirtha. The inner walls of these temples have paintings based on mythological and epic themes.

tirthas.name: Rinmochan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The debt-relieving tirtha of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: In the scriptures, this tirtha is called Rinmochan and Rinpramochan at some places, but its literal meaning is that which frees one from the debts. According to the Brahma Puran, Rinmochan tirtha frees a person from all types of debts, be it Shrauta, Smarta or any other. By taking bath and making donation at this tirtha, the indebted person becomes happy after getting free from debts. The clearance work done in the tank of this tirthas have yielded to sculptures of Vishnu of 9th-10th century CE. These sculptures are presently on display in Srikrishna Museum, Kurukshetra.

tirthas.name: Suryakund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Suryakunds of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: According to legends, a person who takes bath, worships deities and ancestors and observes fasting here, gets the fruits of performing Agnishtom yajna and attains the world of Surya, the sun god. According to a legend, at this place the great sages worshipped Surya with devotion for attaining the salvation for the warriors killed in the Mahabharata war. There are Late medieval bathing ghats with octagonal turrets at this tirtha. The wall paintings in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple may be seen here.

tirthas.name: Vishnupad Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Bali and Vamanaa
tirthas.description: It is said that Lord Vishnu resides here in the form of Vaman. Bali had asked Vaman that by what method he will be able to remember Him continuously residing in the Paatal Lok. Then Vaman had told him that charity given without rituals, Shraddha without Brahmin and Havan done without faith have been destined for you in the netherworld. According to the Mahabharata, one who worships Lord Vaman after taking bath in the waters of this tirtha gets free from all sins and attains the world of Lord Vishnu.

tirthas.name: Juhomi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to sage Juhomi
tirthas.description: The land of Kurukshetra has been a place of penances for many sages and saints. According to popular folklore, this tirtha is named after sage Juhomi where he had undertook penances for a long time. A large number of devotees come to this tirtha for taking sacred bath on the day Amavasya in general and on Solar Eclipse in particular. A Late medieval ghat made of lakhori bricks and having octagonal turrets adorn the tank of this tirtha. It has three arched chambers on both sides of the main entrance.

tirthas.name: Chakra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Mahabharata episode
tirthas.description: According to Brahma Puran, this is a great tirtha where a person attains the world of Vishnu by taking bath with devotion. It is said that in the war between Yam and Indra, Lord Vishnu had sent his Sudarshan Chakra to protect Yama, the god of death. For this reason, this tirtha is known as Chakra tirtha. According to folklore, Bhima's grandson Barbarik watched the entire eighteen days Mahabharata war from his severed head placed here on a pillar.

tirthas.name: Havya Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Brahma's Yajna
tirthas.description: According to popular belief, Brahma had organized a yajya here in the Satyuga in which all the gods and goddesses were invited and fed. The word Havya means the substance offered as an offering. It is said that the Pandavas also lived at this place for some time during their exile. Magnificent ghats of Late medieval times adorn the tank of this tirtha. Floral ornamentation on the interior of the temple located at the tirtha is attractive.

tirthas.name: Rasamangal Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Yaksha tirthas of Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to folklore, a special yajna was organized by Brahma at this tirtha, in which he invited all the gods and goddesses. Brahma offered Som Rasa to the gods which was their favorite drink. In many folklores this tirtha is related to Yaksha. Medieval potteries and bricks have been found from an ancient mound in the tirtha complex. This also reveals the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Sri Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: A tirtha dedicated to goddess Lakshmi
tirthas.description: This tirtha bestows people with opulence, wealth and prosperity. According to the Mahabharata, a person who visits this tirtha and takes bath in waters of this tirtha with a restrained heart and worships the gods and ancestors, attains immense wealth and prosperity. It is mentioned in Narada Purana that a person who takes a bath at Sri tirtha and worships Sri Hari finds deity's present near him every day. The walls of the temple are decorated with paintings.

tirthas.name: Vaman Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Vamanaa tirthas of Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, a person who visits this tirtha related to incarnation of Lord Vishnu, gets freed from all sins and attains the world of Vishnu. According to Vaman Puran, Lord Vishnu took the form of Vaman here and abducted the kingdom of King Bali and gave it to Indra. There are many wall paintings made in the temple situated here, in which the prominent ones are Vishnu reclining on Sheshnaga, birth of Brahma from the navel lotus of Vishnu, Hanuman, Raaslila, Matsya Avatar etc.

tirthas.name: Kukrityanashan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Sin eradicating tirtha
tirthas.description: Legends associate this tirtha with Kunti, the mother of Pandavas. This tirtha had such an influence that many sages and saints performed penances here and made it more sacred. Probably due to the power of their penances, this tirtha was able to destroy the evil deeds of living beings. According to the popular belief among the common people, many living beings also remain engaged in penances here, which ultimately increases the positive vibrations of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Anyajanma Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to the incarnations of Shiva and Vishnu
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Narasimha, the incarnation of Vishnu and Sharabha, incarnation of Shiva. It is said that Narasimha was transformed into Shaligram and Sharabh into Linga at this tirtha. This tirtha is called Ambajanma in Mahabharata and Anyajanma in the Vamana Purana. According to the Mahabharata, a person who takes bath and sacrifices his life in this tirtha, attains the best worlds with the will of sage Narad. A person who performs oblation of water for ancestors here gets knowledge related to the senses.

tirthas.name: Navdurga Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the tirthas dedicated to mother goddess
tirthas.description: According to popular tradition, this place named Devigarh could not be inhabited due to outbreak of floods every year. The Goddess appeared in the dream of a sage and said that if the idol of goddess Durga is installed at this place, then this place will be properly inhabited and everyone will be blessed. After this, the Navdurga temple was built here. The temple located here has a beautiful depiction of Raaslila with floral decoration.

tirthas.name: Devi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the tirthas dedicated to mother goddess
tirthas.description: This tirtha is one of the famous Devi tirthas of Kurukshetra region. It is mentioned in the Mahabharata and Vaman Puran. According to the Mahabharata, a person who is devoted and has controlled his senses, gets the fruits of performing Agnishtom yajna by visiting this tirtha. According to Vaman Puran, Bhadra, Nidra, Maya, Sanatani and Katyayani forms of goddess Durga are always present here. A person who takes bath in the waters of this tirtha and sees goddess Durga, undoubtedly gets rid of mundane troubles.

tirthas.name: Vriddhakedar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the major Shaivite tirthas of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: This tirtha is described as Kapisthal in the Vaman Puran and Mahabharata. Probably the corrupted form of Kapisthal became famous as Kaithal over time. The name Kapisthal is also confirmed by the location of the famous south-facing Hanuman temple in the tirtha complex. According to Vaman Puran, one gets the benefits of visiting the pilgrimages of Kedarnath and Varanasi by visiting this tirtha. The Shraddha performed here on the Chaturdashi of the Shukla Paksha of Chaitra month is considered as highly meritorious.

tirthas.name: Gyaraha Rudri tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to the eleven Rudras
tirthas.description: This tirtha is dedicated to the eleven Rudras named Mrigvyadh, Nirriti, Ajaikpad, Dahan, Ishwar, Kapali, Sthanu, Bhag, Sarp, Ahirbudh and Pinaki. It is mentioned in Vishnu Purana that Brahma had disposed the eleven Rudras at eleven places of the heart here. According to folklore, at the end of the Mahabharata war, Ashwatthama had worshipped Lord Shiva at this place before attacking the camp of Pandavas at night. Religious and secular paintings may be seen on the inner walls of the temple.

tirthas.name: Aahn Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Surya
tirthas.description: This tirtha is mentioned by the name Ahna in the Rigveda, Mahabharata and Vaman Puran. Probably this Ahna tirthas became famous as Aahn over times. The Mahabharata refers two tirthas named Ahna and Sudin most famous on the earth. And a person who takes bath in the waters of these tirthas attains the world of Surya. In the Vaman Puran also, importance of this tirtha has been emphasized.

tirthas.name: Ramsharan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to an episode of Mahabharata war
tirthas.description: According to folklore, after Abhimanyu's martyrdom, Jayadratha hid at this place out of fear of Arjuna. Probably this is the same place where Jayadratha was hidden in the Chakra-Shakat Vyuha created by Dronacharya on the fourteenth day of Mahabharata war. There are Late medieval bathing ghats with octagonal turrets at the tirtha. This tirtha is located near the palaeochannel of the River Drishadvati. Potteries and other artefacts of Early historic period to medieval period have been found from the fields to the south of the tirtha. At present, a modern Hanuman temple with Nagar Shikhara is located at the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Jyeshthashram Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Lord Vishnu
tirthas.description: In the Vaman Puran, it is said that by performing Shraddha, donation, fasting at Jyeshthashram and Vishnupad tanks according to rules, one gets imperishable merits. The tirtha is said to be the destroyer of all sins. There is a tradition of fasting on the day of Ekadashi of Shukla Paksha falling in the month of Jyeshth and taking a holy bath on the day of Dwadashi at this tirtha. At this village three other tirthas- Vishnuhrad, Koti tirtha and Surya tirtha also exist. Archaeological remains from Late Harappan to Gupta period has been found from the village Bodshyam.

tirthas.name: Manojav Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated in Vyas van
tirthas.description: This tirtha is situated in Vyas van, one of the seven major forests of ancient Kurukshetra region. According to the Vaman Puran, after taking bath in the waters of this tirtha, one should have a sight of Lord Shiva, the jewel among the gods. Later, this tirtha became famous as Manokamana tirtha, which fulfils the wishes of the devotees. There is a Samadhi temple dedicated to Swami Jagdishanand in the tirtha premises. A well of Kushan period has been found near the tank of the tirtha, which proves the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Kulotaran Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Salvation ensuring tirtha of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: According to the Vaman Puran, this tirtha was established by Lord Vishnu for the people who follow the Varnashram Dharma. According to the Puran twenty-one generations of devotees are liberated by taking a dip in the waters of this tirtha. The tirtha is mentioned in the Mahabharata as Kulampun, which is considered one of the salvation ensuring tirtha of this land. Archaeological remains of medieval period have been found here. The structure on the bathing ghat of the tirtha tank have wall paintings.

tirthas.name: Shakumbhari Devi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to Goddess Shakumbhari
tirthas.description: This tirtha is situated on the bank of River Drishadvati, a tributary of River Saraswati. According to folklore, before the Mahabharata war, a gate was built here for welcoming Srikrisha and Pandavas in the land of Kurukshetra. The temple located in the tirtha is dedicated to Goddess Shakumbhari. There are many Samadhi temples of the sages of Giri sect in the tirthas complex. Remains of Late Harappan and Painted Grey Ware culture are found in the vicinity of the of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Dhundiraj Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Ganesha
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Ganesha which must have been one of the rare temples of Lord Ganesha in this region in the past. In ancient India, Ganesha worshippers were called Ganapatyas which were included in five major sects- Sauras, Vaishnavas, Shaktas and Shaivas. At present, this tirtha is also known as Ram Kundi. According to popular beliet, a person who takes bath in this tirtha tank becomes free from all obstacles. Remains of Late Harappan culture have been reported from the vicinity of the tirthas.

tirthas.name: Arogya Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha known for the treatment of paralysis
tirthas.description: According to local belief, this tirthas is the place of penance of saint Mast Giri who is known for the treatment of paralysis. This tirtha is also known as Dera Saudapur. Remains of late Harappan, Painted Grey Ware, Early historic and medieval artefacts have been found from the vicinity of this tirtha. Remains of brick temple of 7th-8th century CE are located in the nearby village Sitamai.

tirthas.name: Yayati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Chandravanshi King Yayati
tirthas.description: Popular belief associate this tirthas with king Yayati, the remote ancestor of Kaurava, Pandava and Yadavas. He pleased Saraswati by performing many yajnas in the land of Kurukshetra. According to folklore, food was prepared here for the armies of Pandavas during the war of Mahabharata.
