About one km to the north-west of the village, a mound is located which has yielded the remains of Late Harappan, Painted Grey Ware, Early historic and Medieval periods.

tirthas.name: Akshayavat Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with ancestors and divinities
tirthas.description: The donation given at this tirtha for ancestors is considered everlasting. Hence it is called Akshayavat tirtha. According to the Vayu Puran, a person who visits Akshayavat tirtha and worships Brahmins and offers them Havya and Kavya, all the gods including his ancestors get satisfied. In the Brahma Puran, it has been called the place of penance of sage Pulastya. It is also said that due to being indestructible, it became famous as Akshayavat and the people who visit and remember this tirtha get the merits of performing yajna.

tirthas.name: Anjani Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Place related to Anjani, the mother of Hanuman
tirthas.description: It is said that this tirtha belongs to the times of Ramayana where Anjani, the mother of Hanuman did penance. The village Anjanthali in fact is named after her. According to folk belief, a monkey comes here to take bath on every second Tuesday. Village folk look at him as Hanuman. According to folk beliefs, if the water of this tirtha is used for farming, then the crop dries up. The remains of a stone doorjamb of 9th-10th century CE have been found from the tirtha premises, which proves the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Som Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Som tirthas of ancient Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: In the Mahabharata, this tirtha has been called provider of Som Lok or the world of Som deity. The importance of taking sacred bath here has been described same in the Vaman Puran and Mahabharata. According to the Vaman Puran, bathing in the Som tirtha provides the merits of performing Rajsuya yajna. The sacred bath here also destroys the diseases and defects of the devotees. It is said that thirteen saints had taken alive Samadhi here in the past.

tirthas.name: Vishnupad/Vamanak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirthas related to Lord Vaman
tirthas.description: This is fourth tirtha located in the village Bodshyam. It is famous as Vishnuhrad, Vishnupad or Vamanak tirtha. It is said in the Mahabharata that one should take bath in the Vishnupad and worship Lord Vaman. In the Vaman Puran it is related to Vaman incarnation as well as king Bali. According to this Puran, by bathing and making most of the donation here on the day of Ekadashi of the Shukla Paksha of the month of Jyeshtha, the devotee attains the supreme position. Evidences of different cultures from the Late Harappan to historical periods have been found from the vicinity of this place.

tirthas.name: Surya Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Surya
tirthas.description: This is the third tirtha located in Bodshyam village. It is dedicated to Surya, the Sun deity. A person who bathes in the waters of the tank with devotion is considered great in the world of Surya. Sun worship has been of special importance in Kurukshetra region since ancient times. There is an ancient tradition of bathing in the Surya Kunds of this land on the occasion of solar eclipse. The remains of many ancient cultures have been found from Bodshyam village.

tirthas.name: Koti Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Lord Shiva
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Lord Shiva. The importance of this tirtha is described in the Vaman Puran in such a way that a person who bathes in the tank of this tirtha gets the merits of performing crores of yajnas. The devotee dedicated to the tirtha gets the title of Gananayak after visiting Kotishwar Mahadev here. The presence of three other tirthas named Jyeshthashram, Vishnuhrad and Surya Tirtha has also been reported from the village. Archaeological remains of Late Harappan, Painted Grey Ware, Maurya, Shunga, Kushan and Gupta period have been found from its ancient mound.

tirthas.name: Brahma Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with Brahma
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, by taking bath in the waters of this tirtha, a non-Brahmin attains brahminhood. In the Brahma Puran, this tirtha is mentioned along with Samantak Panchak tirtha. In this Puran, this tirtha is said to be rare even for the gods. It is said that this tirtha provides enjoyment, prosperity and salvation to the human beings. The bathing ghats of the tank of the tirtha are made of Late medieval lakhori bricks comprising octagonal turrets.

tirthas.name: Prokshni/Pranita Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha bearing similarity to ritual-pot called Prokshni
tirthas.description: A temple made of lakhori bricks at the tirtha is called Mata ka Mandir. Near the tank the Samadhi of Gausain Baba who took alive Samadhi here exists. This tirtha is mainly associated with saints. It is believed that if the milch animals stop giving milk, they start giving milk again by bathing them in the tank of this tirtha. In ancient times, some Siddha made this place his seat of penance. This tirtha has been made in the shape of Prokshni, a ritual-pot.

tirthas.name: Sudin and Narvada Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha located on an ancient mound
tirthas.description: This tirtha is situated on an ancient archaeological mound known as Omkar Ka Khera. In the Mahabharata and mythological literature, this tirtha is described as rare sacred spot where a devotee who visits attains the Surya Lok or the world of Surya. This proves that this tirtha must have been dedicated to the Surya or Sun deity. Remains from the Late Harappan to the Gupta period are found from this mound. Tirtha temple contains wall paintings on religious themes.

tirthas.name: Kaushiki Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Mahabharata war
tirthas.description: A reference of the tirtha is found in the Vana Parva of Mahabharata where it is mentioned after Rudrakoti Tirtha. According to local belief, water was supplied to the armies from here during the Mahabharata war. Out of the seven wells of ancient times, only three wells are seen here now. In the past, the water of this tirtha was considered as pure and clean as the water of River Ganga. In Late medieval times, there was a hermitage of the famous saint Baba Dayalpuri, whose samadhi-temple stands along with the Shiva temple in the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Vedvati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tritha existed during Ramayana era
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Sita who was Vedvati in her previous birth. According to folklore, Sita has entered into the earth at this place. It is said in the Vaman Puran that by taking bath here, a person gets the merits of performing Kanya Yajna and gets rid of all sins and attains the supreme position. The lower part of the temple located at the tirtha is made of moulded bricks is comparable with the brick temple of Kalayat (district Kaithal) dated to 7th-8th century CE.

tirthas.name: Vimalsar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha leading to Rudra Lok
tirthas.description: This tirtha is one of the Shaiv tirthas of Kurukshetra region. According to Vaman Puran, a person who takes bath in the waters of this tirtha attains Rudra Lok. It is also said in the Mahabharata that by taking bath in this excellent tirtha, a person soon attains Indra Lok and gets salvation by purifying himself from all sins. Proto historic potteries and bricks have been found in the tirtha complex and remains of a well of Late Harappan period have been found in the village Sagga.

tirthas.name: Parashar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Place of penances related to sage Parashar
tirthas.description: According to folklore, sage Parashar had organized a yajna in which thousands of demons were burnt to death. Then sage Vashishtha and Pulastya etc. stopped his yajna. Later sage Vyasa as the son of sage Parashar was born from his wife Satyavati who composed the Mahabharata and eighteen Puranas. Remains from the Late Harappan to the Early historic period are found in the tirthas complex. Walls of the temples comprise the paintings related to religious themes.

tirthas.name: Prithvi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha of Ramayana era
tirthas.description: The religious importance of this tirtha is described in the Mahabharata. Here it is said that by visiting this tirtha, one gets the merits of donating a thousand cows. The Vaman Puran also clearly mentions the religious importance of this tirtha and says that all sins committed on the earth are destroyed by taking a sacred bath in waters of this tirtha. Popular belief also considers it to be the place of penances of sage Valmiki, the author of the Ramayana epic.

tirthas.name: Vyas-sthali
tirthas.shortDescription: Seat of penance related to sage Veda Vyasa
tirthas.description: This tirth named Vyas-sthali is related to sage Vyasa who was the son of sage Parashar and the editor of the Mahabharata epic and Puranas. It is mentioned that sage Vyasa started to live at this place after being saddened as his son Shukdeva who had abandoned the world. Since then it was named as Vyas-sthali. According to the Mahabharata, bathing and making donation here gives the merits of donating thousands of cows. It is also said that by visiting this tirtha a person never has to mourn the separation of his son.

tirthas.name: Trigunanand Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to sage Gautama and Dronacharya
tirthas.description: According to popular belief, sage Gautama performed penance at this place. As per the Mahabharata evidence, sage Gautama along with other had a pleasant stay here on Arjuna's birthday. According to the Drona Parva of Mahabharata sage Gautama made a request to Acharya Drona to stop the war of Mahabharata at this place. The octagonal-shaped turrets of late medieval period exist on the ghat of the tirtha tank.

tirthas.name: Chucchukarandav Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to saints
tirthas.description: This tirtha is dedicated to the saints whose temple exists adjacent to the modern temple. The sanctum sanctorum of the temple contains an image of Lord Vishnu of Pratihara period (9th-10th century CE) along with some modern images. This indicates the existence of a temple of medieval period at this place in the past. Samadhis of many Naga Sadhus are locaed in the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Pavan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha providing the merit of performing Agnistom yajna
tirthas.description: This tirtha is mentioned in the Mahabharata after Swastipur. Visit the tirtha and offering of tarpan to the deities and ancestors is considered equivalent to performing Agnishtom yajna. In the Mahabharata itself, under Anushasana Parva, Pavan has been counted among one of the Vishwadevas. Popular tradition mentions it as a tirtha of the time of Pandavas. The people here believe that the wishes of the devotees are fulfilled after visiting here. The villagers also call this tirtha as Gopalmochan.

tirthas.name: Jambunad Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha which ensure success in life
tirthas.description: Of the many tirthas mentioned in the Mahabharata and the Puranas, by visiting the Jambunad tirtha a person gets merits of performing Ashwamedha Yajna. As per scripture, the tirtha is also visited by the deities, sages and forefathers. It also finds mention as Jambukeshwar in the Agni Puran and Kurma Puran. Sage Vyasa also visited this tirtha considering its importance.

tirthas.name: Jarasandh Ka Tila
tirthas.shortDescription: The site of an ancient Buddhist Stupa
tirthas.description: The archaeological mound is identified with ancient city of Assandh. Popular belief associate the site with king Jarasandh of the Mahabharata period. It is said that the city named Asandhivat was the second capital of the Pandavas. Asandhiwat was a prosperous city at the time of king Janmejaya, the son of king Parikshit. Jarasandh's mound is actually the lower part of a huge Buddhist stupa which is built with Kushan bricks of Ist century CE.

tirthas.name: Dhanakshetra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The seat of penances of many sages and seers
tirthas.description: According to popular belief, the name of this tirtha is Dhanakshetra which has been the seat of penances of many sages and seers over the ages. It is still important due to their blessings. According to popular belief, one who takes a Parikrama of the Samadhi situated in the tirtha brings very auspicious results and all pending works of a person get completed. By taking a Parikrama here, the animals which have stopped giving milk start giving milk again, Late medieval lakhori bricks are found in the surroundings of the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Phalgu Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The second tirthas of of Kurukshetra region dedicated to sage Phalgu
tirthas.description: According to the Vayu Puran, a person should visit Phalgu tirtha, the best among all the tirthas. Those who perform Shraddha here, their ancestors always get salvation. In ancient times, on the request of Brahma, Lord Vishnu himself appeared in the form of Phalgu here. Regarding the greatness of this tirtha, it is said that even a person who performs one lakh Ashvamedha yajnas does not get as much benefit as the one who takes bath in the waters of Phalgu tirtha.

tirthas.name: Brahm Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the tirthas related to Brahma
tirthas.description: This is one of the tirtha related to Brahma in the land of Kurukshetra. According to the Vaman Puran, Brahma had worshipped Lord Shiva here with devotion to atone for his sins. Pleased with Brahma's devotion, Shiva ordered him to establish four lingas. Then Brahma, who was freed from sins, established four lingas on the land of Kurukshetra out of which one was installed here. It is believed that by merely seeing this linga, a person attains the ultimate salvation. Tirtha premises contains the architectural fragments of a temple dating 9th-10th century CE.

tirthas.name: Dashashwamedha Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha which ensures the merits of performing ten Ashwamedha Yajnas
tirthas.description: This tirtha is located on the bank of River Drishadvati, which anciently flowed on the eastern border of Kurukshetra region. This tirthas has been mentioned by the name Shalukini in the Van Parva of Mahabharata. According to the Mahabharata, by bathing and making charity here, a person gets the fruits of performing ten Ashvamedha Yajnas. It has been said in the Vayu Puran that by performing Shraddha at the tirtha named Dashashwamedha and Panchashwamedha, one gets the merits of performing ten and five Ashwamedha yajnas. Late medieval temple and ghats of the tirtha are embelished with wall paintings.

tirthas.name: Koti Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: A sacred spot created to contain waters of various tirthas
tirthas.description: The Brahma Puran refers to a Koti Koot tirtha which the local people identify with Karori tirtha. It is said that a sage had stored waters from crores of tirthas in his kamandal. As soon as he put a drop of water from this tirtha into his kamanadal, his kamandal fell down. Then the sage understood the importance of this tirtha and declared that this tirtha comprises the waters of crores of tirthas which existed on the earth.

tirthas.name: Panchadev Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: This tirtha is associated with five cult deities of Sanatan Dharma
tirthas.description: This tirtha is associated with five cult deities of Sanatan Dharma. Shiva, Vishnu, Devi, Surya and Ganesha shrines dedicated to these deities may have existed at this place. At present, the shrines named Ramkundhi, Shyorgarhi and Dera Santram are present in the tirthas complex. These would have been representing the continuity of ancient cults at this site.

tirthas.name: Jamdagni Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with sage Jamdagni
tirthas.description: This tirtha related to sage Jamdagni, the father of Parashurama was according to folklore, the place where his hermitage stood and lived with wife Renuka and his sons. His son Parashurama was a great devotee of his father who was forced to kill his mother on the orders of his father. After getting a boon from his father, he revived his mother again, It is also said that Parashurama started his struggle against the unjust Kshatriyas from here.

tirthas.name: Gautam Rishi/Gavendra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with sage Gautama
tirthas.description: This tirtha associated with sage Gautam who is counted among the seven great sages. He is mentioned in the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Due to curse of Gautama, his wife Ahalya turned into a rock. According to the Uttara Ramayana, Lakshman, the younger brother of Lord Rama built a grand palace near the hermitage of sage Gautam. Tirtha premises comprises the Samadhi temples of sages of Giri sect. The temple dedicated to Lord Shiva at the tirthas comprises the wall paintings based on religious theme.

tirthas.name: Daksheshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with the marriage of Sati and Shiva
tirthas.description: According to the Vaman Puran that a devotee who sees Daksheshwar Shiva at this place gets the merits of performing Ashwamedha yajna. According to popular belief, the marriage ceremony of Shiva and Sati took place here. As mention in the Mahabharata the Pandavas visited this place during their exile period. Roof of a Late medieval temple standing at the tirtha has been embellished with floral depiction.

tirthas.name: Jamdagni Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with sage Jamdagni
tirthas.description: This tirtha related to sage Jamdagni, the father of Parashurama was according to folklore, the place where his hermitage stood and lived with wife Renuka and his sons. His son Parashurama was a great devotee of his father who was forced to kill his mother on the orders of his father. After getting a boon from his father, he revived his mother again, It is also said that Parashurama started his struggle against the unjust Kshatriyas from here.

tirthas.name: Gautam Rishi/Gavendra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with sage Gautama
tirthas.description: This tirtha associated with sage Gautam who is counted among the seven great sages. He is mentioned in the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Due to curse of Gautama, his wife Ahalya turned into a rock. According to the Uttara Ramayana, Lakshman, the younger brother of Lord Rama built a grand palace near the hermitage of sage Gautam. Tirtha premises comprises the Samadhi temples of sages of Giri sect. The temple dedicated to Lord Shiva at the tirthas comprises the wall paintings based on religious theme.

tirthas.name: Dashrath/Raghavendra Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha which existed during the Ramayana era
tirthas.description: This tirtha related to the time of Ramayana is supposed to have been built by king Dashratha of Ayodhya. Due to this reason, it is known as Dashrath or Raghavendra tirtha. Being childless, king Dashratha, on the advice of sage Vasishtha, the family priest of solar dynasty of Ayodhya built this tirtha to get the offspring. The tank of the tirtha have Late medieval ghat adorn with octagonal turrets.

tirthas.name: Mishrak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha associated with sages Ved Vyas and Dadhichi
tirthas.description: This tirtha named Mishrak contains waters of many sacred tirthas. In the Vaman Puran, sage Vyasa had done this pious act for sage Dadhichi. According to the Mahabharata, the waters of many tirthas was collected here by the sage Ved Vyasa for the sake of Brahmins. According to the Vaman Puran, bathing in the tank of this tirtha bestows the merits of bathing in all the tirthas existing on the earth. The temple at tirtha contains modern paintings related to religious themes.

tirthas.name: Govind Kund
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the five tanks related to Parashurama
tirthas.description: Govind Kund is situated on the bank of the ancient River Drishadvati situated on the border line of 48 Kos Kurukshetra region. This tirtha is counted among those five Kunds along with Ramhrad, Sannihit, Surya Kund and Kalyani which were created by Parashuram. Today, all of them are regarded salvation ensuring tirthas. Late medieval temples and ghats stand at the tirtha. A grand Gita Updesh Rath has been installed in the middle of the tirtha tank. Medieval remains are found from the tirtha complex.

tirthas.name: Parashar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to sage Parashara
tirthas.description: Folklore connects this tirtha with sage Parashara who was the grandson of sage Vashishtha and father of sage Ved Vyas. This tirtha is also famous by the name of Pagdhoi. It is said that during the Mahabharata war, Lord Krishna stayed here for some time and washed his feet with the waters of this tirtha On every Amavasya, milk is donated from every household of the village for making the prasad at this tirtha. Medieval pottery has been found from the tirtha and Early historic and medieval remains have also been found from a nearby village called Panju Khurd to the west of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Soham Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to sage Dattatreya
tirthas.description: According to folk belief, worshipping Dattatreya at this tirtha leads to unique enlightenment. The deity of the tirtha is a Siras tree which is worshipped here. Devotees use to pour water in its roots. Situated on the boundary line of the land of 48 Kos Kurukshetra region, this tirtha is situated on the palaeochannel of the ancient River Drishadvati. Early medieval potteries and other archaeological remains are found from the fields of the village.

tirthas.name: Chausath Yogini Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated on the palaeochannel of River Drishadvati
tirthas.description: This tirtha is dedicated to the sixty-four Yoginis, who are usually worshipped in the south-east corner along with the Navagrahas. The joint temple located here is dedicated to the sixty-four Yoginis and a sage named Bhai Ji. The top of the temple comprises the images of four out of the sixty-four Yoginis who could not answer the questions asked by Bhai Ji and since then stayed here at the tirtha. The name of village Kalavati also seems to have been named after one of the Yoginis. There stands a Late medieval bathing ghat on the tank of the tirtha. Sacred bath in the tirtha tank is taken on the tenth day of every month in Shukla Paksha.

tirthas.name: Mallikeshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Shaiv tirtha located on the bank of River Drishadvati
tirthas.description: This tirtha is situated on the bank of the River Drishadvati, a tributary of River Saraswati. According to folklore, this tirtha is known as Mallikeshwar tirtha, which is one of the name of Lord Shiva. Folk tales relate this tirtha to Lord Krishna who had stationed Arjuna's chariot at this place. According to another folk belief, this village is named after Dhritarashtra. Archaeological remains of Kushan and Gupta period have been found from the village mound. A fragment of doorjamb depicting goddess Ganga of 9th-10th century CE has also been found from this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Lokoddhar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The place associated with sage Lauha
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Lord Vishnu because he liberates the three worlds, hence it is named Lokoddhar tirtha. According to the Mahabharata, a devotee who wants to know the essence of Dharma liberates his loved ones by taking sacred bath in the waters of this tirtha. According to the Vaman Puran, a person can liberate his near and dear ones by taking bath in this tirtha which is revered in the three worlds. It is a popular belief that sage Lauha also performed sever penance here.

tirthas.name: Kush/Ramsar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Seat of penance of sage Kush
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, a sage named Kush who was as glorious as the fire god (Agni). Had performed rigorous penance for a long time at this tirtha. In the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata reference of two tirthas named Kushastamba and Kushavart is found. These may have been connected with this tirtha. Samadhi of Baba Brahmadas is built in the tirtha premises.

tirthas.name: Kayashodhan Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The tirtha that purifies the human body
tirthas.description: According to the Mahabharata, there remains no doubt in purifying the body of a person who takes sacred bath in the waters of Kayashodhan tirtha. According to the Vaman Puran, by taking bath in this tirtha, a person gets freed from the cycle of birth and death. The Purana further state that, after visiting this tirtha, there is no need to visit any other tirthas. It is said that the leprosy of the king of Patiala was also cured after bathing in this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Vanshmoolak Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to redeeming of lineage
tirthas.description: This tirtha is famous for redeeming the lineage of the people. According to the Mahabharata, a person who takes bath in the waters of this tirtha, gets his lineage redeemed. According to the Vaman Puran, a person who controls his senses properly, visits the Vanshmoolak tirtha and takes sacred bath there, gets success for his lineage. Ancient sculptures of Gandharvas and Kinnaras of 9th-10th century CE are installed on the façade of a temple which exists here. This proves the antiquity of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Sarpadhi Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: A tirtha dedicated to Nagas
tirthas.description: This tirtha is mentioned in the Mahabharata as Sarpadevi and in the Vaman Puran as Sarpaddhi. According to the Mahabharata, on visiting this best Nag tirtha, a person gets the fruit of performing Agnishtom yajna and becomes the owner of the world of Nagas. Traditionally, clarified butter and curd are donated to the snakes here. According to folklore, in this connection the residential arrangements for the participant Brahmins and sages were also made at this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Sarpadman Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Place of serpent sacrifice performed by king Janamejaya
tirthas.description: According to popular belief, to take revenge for his father's death due to snake bite, Janamejaya, the son of king Parikshit in consultation with sages and Brahmins, had performed a huge Sarpadman Yajna at this place to destroy the entire race of serpents. Due to the miraculous effect of the mantras, large and powerful snakes started falling into the sacrificial altar. Finally, the yajna was stopped at the behest of Aastik, the son of sage Jaratkaru. The temples situated at the tirtha were built by the king of Jind dating the Late medieval times.

tirthas.name: Panchanad/Hatakeshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirths related to Ashwatthama
tirthas.description: According to popular belief, it was at this place that Arjuna, on the advice of Lord Krishna, removed the gem from the forehead of Ashwatthama with the tip of his bow and left him bereft of the gem. The image of Ashwatthama is worshipped in the tirtha temple. According to the Vaman Puran, Rudra himself is present here after incorporating crores of tirthas in this tirtha, hence this tirtha is also called Koti tirtha. According to popular belief, the brilliance and power of 68 tirtha of the earth is contained in the sacred tank of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Yayati Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The place of yajna performed by king Yayati
tirthas.description: This tirtha of Kurukshetra region is related to Yayati, the second son of king Nahush. Lord Krishna was born in the lineage of Yadu, who was the son born to king Yayati from his wife Devayani. Kauravas and Pandavas were born in the lineage of Puru, the son of the king Yayati from second wife Sharmishtha. According to the Vaman Puran, River Saraswati poured honey for performing yajna of king Yayati at this tirtha. In this Purana, instead of Yayati, the tirtha has been mentioned by the name of Yayaat.

tirthas.name: Jamdagni Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha situated on the bank of River Drishadvati
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to sage Jamdagni, the great grandson of sage Chyavan. According to popular belief, sage Jamadagni performed severe penance at this tirtha. Once a demon named Haiheyi disturbed his penance and insulted the sage and killed his disciples. The saddened sage got the demon Haiheyi killed by his son Parshuram. This tirtha is counted among the 68 holy places. Remains of Harappan culture are found from the tirtha complex which prove the antiquity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Ashwini Kumar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha dedicated to Ashwini Kumars
tirthas.description: Ashwini tirtha is associated with Ashwini Kumars, the physicians of the divinities. On the request of Sukanya, Ashwini Kumars had given youthful life to her husband sage Chyavan here. Among the five Pandavas, Nakul and Sahadev two Pandava heroes born to Madri, were the sons of Ashwini Kumars. According to the Vaman Puran, a devout and self-controlled person becomes handsome and famous by visiting this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Varaha Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Varaha incarnation of Vishnu
tirthas.description: This tirtha is dedicated to Varaha, the third incarnation of Lord Vishnu. According to the Vaman Puran, a person who takes bath in the waters of this tirtha with devotion becomes entitled for supreme bliss. The tirtha temple has a stone image of Varaha dating 8th-9th century CE. It is a eight-armed image of the deity. This village was named Brah Kalan after the name of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Som Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Somvati Amavasya
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to Som, the moon god in the Mahabharata, Vaman Puran and Padma Puran. According to the Mahabharata, a person gets the fruits of performing Rajsuya Yajna by taking bath in waters of this tirtha situated in Jayanti region (Jind). According to popular belief, Pandavas had waited for twelve years for taking bath here on the occasion of Somvati Amavasya. According to popular belief, after the Mahabharata war, Pandavas had performed Pinda Daan for their ancestors at this place.

tirthas.name: Pushkar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The Yaksha of the south-western corner of Kurukshetra
tirthas.description: In the Vaman Puran, sage Parashuram has been mentioned as the creator of this tirtha which is a seat of Kapil Yaksha. According to Vaman Puran, by visiting the Pushkar tirtha, all the wishes of a person are fulfilled. It is also said that if a king visits this tirtha, he gets the fruits of performing Ashwamedha Yajna. On the day of Kartik Purnima, the person who makes charity here, gets desired boon from the gods.

tirthas.name: Sannihit Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the salvation providing tirthas
tirthas.description: The name and importance of this tirtha is described in detail in the Mahabharata and Vaman Puran. The charity made at this tirtha on the occasion of solar eclipse has special importance. According to popular belief, this tank is the real Sannihit Sarovar and Sannihit tirtha of Thanesar was built later on. According to the Mahabharata, the only touch of this tirtha on the occasion of solar eclipse provides the fruits of performing hundreds of Ashvamedha yajnas to the devotees.

tirthas.name: Ramhrad Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: Tirtha related to Parashurama
tirthas.description: This tirtha is related to sage Parashurama, son of sage Jamadagni, who is counted among the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu. Enraged by the unjust behaviour of the tyrannical and oppressive Kshatriyas, sage Parashurama, destroyed them and filled five tanks at this place with their blood. According to the Mahabharata, by offering tarpan to the ancestors, the devotee gets rare things in the world. It is also said that the decisive duel between Bhima and Duryodhana took place at the shore of this tirtha.

tirthas.name: Ekhans Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: The tank where Duryodhana hid
tirthas.description: Popular belief associates this tirtha with goose incarnation of Lord Vishnu. According to the Mahabharata, a person who bathes in this tirtha gets the fruit of donating thousands of cows. Folklore connects this tirtha with the lake where Duryodhan came to hide in the waters on the eighteenth day of Mahabharata war. Thereafter, Pandavas searched him and challenged for the duel. For this reason this tirtha is also called as Dhundu by the folks. Discovery of the sculptures of 9th-10th century CE recovered from the tirtha premises shows the antiquity of the tirtha.

tirthas.name: Bhuteshwar Tirtha
tirthas.shortDescription: One of the Shaivite tirthas of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: This tirtha is mentioned in the Mahabharata as Jayanti tirtha. In the Vaman Puran, this tirtha is called Bhuteshwar Jwalamaleshwar which comes after Som Tirtha. According to one opinion, the temple built by king of Jind is the real Bhuteshwar Jwalamaleshwar tirtha. According to other opinion, the temple located in nearby Aparahi Mohalla is the real ancient Bhuteshwar Jwalamaleshwar tirtha. According to the Vaman Puran, a person who worships these two Lingas named Bhuteshwar and Jwalamaleshwar is freed from the cycle of birth and death.

tirthas.name: Machruk Yaksha
tirthas.shortDescription: Yaksha of the south-eastern corner of Kurukshetra region
tirthas.description: This tirtha is dedicated to Machruk Yaksha which is one of the four Yakshas mentioned in the Mahabharata. This Yaksha tirtha is located on the bank of River Drishadvati. There is a Yaksha Kund in the tirtha premises. Remains of an ancient temple have been found at the tirtha. Now a modern temple has been constructed over the old structures. Late medieval bathing ghats made of lakhori bricks exist in the tirtha tank.
